reviews.text: I had fun with this. Upgrade your ship and fight thousands of "cute" Aliens until the screen explodes. No frame rate issues for me. A lot going on. Many weapons and items to try out. Survive Space!

I'm older, and it takes something special to pull me into a game. I was hooked on the beta's graphics early on so this was an instant purchase for me. I haven't regretted a cent. Procedural generation has been around for a while, but Cosmic Run uses it well. The roster of playable aliens has different playstyles at heart. The starting alien feels a bit safe, but I'm on the verge of unlocking Zorina. With her spinning ring of drones and increased health regen, she seems great for buzzing crowds and getting away quickly. I'd probably also give her the longer-distance ricochet sled powerup so she can tear into the crowds on approach. As others have noted, there were a lot of crashes at release, but the most recent update seems to have sorted that out for me. The only thing stopping me now is my own skill level. As my first space roguelite, I give this a thumbs up if you want something with visual flair and fun, quick romps.
Fun Action-Rougelite! Fans of the genre will very much enjoy this Game. I did have some crashes on release, but those have since been fixed. I recommend that anyone give the demo a try!
I had some issues when game launched, but finally playing without an issue since the last update! It s one of the rare fun rogue games.
Super fun game for quick sessions inbetween other tasks or a quick round on the side with some nice backgrounds and effects.

Loving the game art, it looks amazing! Its lots of fun to play, has a few small bugs here and there, but nothing too major for me so far at least. I think if we could also use the zogark coins to reroll the weapon/attribute upgrades you get when leveling up could give a bit more control over your loadout. Also perhaps having the only new weapons coming every few set levels and then in between only weapon upgrades. This could help build out a more robust meta gameplay as we could first try rerolling for the right weapons that allows different playstyles and then double down on that by upgrading just that one or two weapons a lot at the beginning. Really looking forward to what updates will come and maybe some new weapons :D

Fun to zip and zoop around! The enemies have very satisfying visual and audio design, and I enjoyed discovering the different weapons/playstyles. I had some minor visual bugs and one crash when starting a new run (not a big deal), and was impressed that I hardly noticed any framerate issues when there are hordes of enemies and my weapons are all blasting off. I liked the family members chatting and encouraging you: I thought it'd bother me that their messages cover part of the screen, but it wasn't an issue at all!

Love the game,artwork is nice, very addicting, honestly can't stop playing it love the different levels and different environments that you are fighting in. Only thing i would change would be level of grinding you need to keep up with so you can progress further it takes a lottt of time haha, other than that pretty cool and fun game. Recommending it to everyone :D

I don't usually post reviews on games nor do I post them early into my playtime, but I had to make an exception for this one. I've played tons of roguelikes and roguelites. They're among my favorite genres of games, but lately they've become saturated with a lot of lazy design and needless complexity. The reason why I'm writing this review this soon is because Cosmic Run doesn't fall victim to this and stands out among the rest in multiple ways. The artstyle is great, a real breath of fresh air. It reminds me of the PS2 era CGi when it was just getting big. It makes the game unique, visually recognizable and striking. The characters are fun, their quips during gameplay are also something I rarely see these days. It adds to worldbuilding, something this genre can struggle with due to how much focus is on gameplay. Gameplay is nothing new by itself, but what I can say is that everything around it is simplified and easily understandable. I'll put it like this, What I really hate about roguelikes/roguelites is when I have to open up 20 stupid wiki articles just to figure out how to optimize a run because descriptions in game don't tell me exactly what a weapon, upgrade or enemy does. Well, Cosmic Run DOES tell you what exactly a weapon or upgrade does and enemies don't need to be explained because you can figure out what they do within the first 15 seconds of encountering them. What adds to this is that runs are relatively short and don't overextend into figuring out how many frame drops you can get by applying 20 different effects to your screen. Simple, quick, easy. Hop in, do a few runs, hop out. I recommend Cosmic Run even after playing it for a relatively short time. I'll continue playing it after this review is posted and I can't wait to see what the devs will bring to the game in future updates. Support this game and the studio. It's worth your time and money.
I absolutely love this game but am becoming frustrated with the constant crashing and locking up with every run. Im not giving up! I'm positive whatever the problem is it will get patched soon!

Cosmic Run grabbed me from the first launch with a simplicity that hides real depth. On the surface it looks like a fast arcade runner through space tunnels, but after a few levels I realised the level design and pacing are carefully honed. The visuals are colorful and stylized—not photorealistic, but a visual language that works perfectly for speed and readability. Neon colors and high-contrast effects give each run tension, and when everything speeds up it’s always clear what matters: obstacles, power-ups and the racing line. The music and sound design are possibly the game’s strongest assets. The soundtrack is dynamic, electronic, and complements the sense of hurtling through space. The music’s tempo often matches level rhythm, so you quickly slip into a flow state and begin reacting almost instinctively. Audio cues for near-misses and pickups are clear and useful, without excessive clutter that would distract. Controls are precise and responsive—which is crucial for this genre. After a quick sensitivity tweak I felt complete control of the ship. Difficulty is well balanced: early levels introduce mechanics, middle sections test precision and reflexes, and later stages demand pattern memorisation and patience. Still, the game rarely feels unfair thanks to a fair checkpoint system and enough progression opportunities. The campaign length isn’t excessive, which works in its favor—each level is designed to be intense and replayable. Replay value is high thanks to leaderboards, challenges and collectables. If you enjoy improving your times and chasing perfect runs, you’ll spend a lot of time returning to the same maps. Regarding bugs, my experience was solid—minor visual artifacts and occasional frame dips occurred on older hardware, but nothing game-breaking. More performance options would help players with weaker machines. Compared to other fast arcade titles (I thought of rhythm-runners like Thumper and stylised runners like Runner3), Cosmic Run combines simplicity and challenge without feeling hollow. It isn’t revolutionary, but it does almost everything it promises—and does it well.
Great visuals and upgrade variety. A bit slow at the start, but definitely a fun time for Roguelite fans.

Not much to this game. It is quite basic and there isn't too much to explore. The meta progression is very minimal and within the 2hrs I've played I have unlocked all the characters and beat 2 out of 3 of the zones. Not sure if there is anything else that will be added to it at all or not, but I surely wouldn't pay full price for a game with as little content as this. I got it 50% off and I still feel like that was a bit of a ripoff. I may change this review if something more shows up down the line, but as of right now it is hard to recommend to anyone when you can get many more games with some real content and gameplay value for the price.
Another survivor-like set in space. It feels a bit disconnected, having no enemies really shooting at you, and weapons that don't really jive well with the gameplay.
Fully playable on Deck; Runs well, gamepad support, no issues whatsoever!
